parties.counterparty: TrueLink, Inc. (Vendor — licensor and hosting provider)

plans.note: No dedicated limitation-of-liability heading appears in the supplied outline, but the outline skips numbers (3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13+), so a cap may sit in an unlisted section or be embedded in the indemnity at sec-12. Check sec-12 for damages exclusions/caps before concluding it is missing; confirm mutuality and carve-outs for confidentiality (sec-10) and IP indemnity.

Sec-12 INDEMNITY is the primary target: confirm TrueLink indemnifies Client for third-party IP infringement and its own misconduct, and that any Client-side indemnity (possibly tied to the covenants in sec-8 or the e-mail obligations in sec-7) stays narrow and is not the only indemnity in the agreement.

Restrictions on Client's business would most plausibly appear in sec-8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) or as a field-of-use restriction in the sec-2 licence. Nothing in the outline signals a non-compete; treat as absent unless sec-8 contains a business-restraint covenant.

Hosting/licensing deals of this type often make TrueLink the exclusive host or require Client to route all mortgage web traffic through it. Look for exclusivity language in sec-2 (licence scope) and sec-8 (Client covenants); sec-5 may tie compensation to exclusive volume.

Any most-favoured-pricing language would live in sec-5 COMPENSATION. Only flag if the MFN runs against us (Client obliged to give TrueLink its best terms); an MFN in Client's favour is welcome and must not be redlined.

A non-solicit binding Client would sit in sec-8 covenants or be appended to the confidentiality provisions at sec-10. If present, verify it is time-limited (12–24 months), employee-only, and carves out general advertising; a mutual or vendor-only non-solicit needs no comment.

No term/termination section appears in the supplied outline; the numbering gaps suggest one may exist unlisted. Flag as missing only after confirming no termination provision elsewhere — we need Client termination for convenience on notice without penalty, and no mid-term vendor walk-away.

Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice would normally accompany a term clause, which is not in the supplied outline; sec-5 is the only place price-uplift-on-renewal language might surface. Treat as absent pending review of unlisted sections.

No governing law/dispute resolution heading in the supplied outline — likely in an unlisted miscellaneous section. Accepted: New York, Delaware, California, or England and Wales with court venue; foreign arbitration is a deviation.

No assignment heading supplied; check any unlisted general/miscellaneous provisions. We need affiliate and successor assignment rights for Client and no TrueLink termination right triggered by our change of control.

Direction-sensitive: confirm sec-2 and the sec-1 definitions leave Client owning its content, customer/borrower data and any deliverables it pays for, with no assignment or licence-back of Client IP or data to TrueLink beyond what is needed to provide the Hosting Services; sec-10 may govern data as Confidential Information.

Sec-2 LICENSE is the core clause: test whether the grant extends to Client affiliates and contractors, and whether it is revocable at will, terminable at TrueLink's discretion, or narrowed by definitions in sec-1 (e.g. 'Hosting Services').

Audit/inspection rights over Client usage or records would attach to sec-8 covenants or the sec-5 payment mechanics. If present, require reasonable notice, annual frequency, off-site review where possible, and vendor-borne cost.

Direction-sensitive: check sec-5 for late fees or stipulated damages payable by Client, and sec-7 (unsolicited commercial e-mail) for per-message penalties or fixed sums charged to Client — those are the likely liquidated-damages hooks. Credits running to Client are fine.

Sec-8 covers warranties of Client only; the outline shows no TrueLink performance warranty or service-level commitment. Confirm whether an unlisted section carries vendor warranties/disclaimers before recording as missing — we need a meaningful warranty period with a repair/re-perform or refund remedy.

No insurance heading in the supplied outline. TrueLink hosts our site and handles consumer mortgage data, so standard coverages (commercial general liability, tech E&O/cyber) should be added if genuinely absent.

Sec-5 COMPENSATION is where minimum fees, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay commitments would appear; sec-8 may contain a corresponding Client covenant. Only a commitment without an exit is a deviation.

No exit/transition heading supplied. Given TrueLink hosts the site, we need return of Client data in usable form and reasonable migration assistance at termination; sec-10 may only require destruction of Confidential Information, which is not a substitute for data return.
